_comment: Accepted false positives for Weaver-Free GitHub code scanning alerts. Auditor: scripts/audit-code-scanning.ts. Add entries only for confirmed false positives — not for accepted risks. Accepted risks must be tracked in business/legal/SECURITY-AUDIT.md instead.

dismissed.reason: CodeQL does not parse TypeScript 5.x cast syntax (as unknown as {...} on line 139). File typechecks clean with vue-tsc. Not a real syntax error.

HTTP response is (1) size-bounded at MAX_REMOTE_CATALOG_BYTES, (2) Zod-schema-validated before any write, and (3) written to a config-controlled path, not a user-supplied one. CodeQL taint analysis cannot reason through schema.parse() so this fires as a false positive.

The cache read already uses the readFile-with-ENOENT-fallthrough pattern that CodeQL's rule prescribes. The slug is validated against the COMPLIANCE_DOCS whitelist before any path construction. CodeQL cannot reason through the whitelist check so this fires as a false positive.

The rule's own message — 'Insecure creation of file in the os temp dir' — is factually false here. `os.tmpdir()` occurs EXACTLY ONCE in backend/src (compliance-pdf.ts:94) and this module does not reference it. atomicWriteJson writes `${filePath}.tmp-<hex>` beside its DESTINATION, deliberately, so rename(2) stays atomic on one filesystem; every caller (json-registry, audit-store, catalog-store, distro-store, url-validator) passes a path under the configured dataDir. Verify with: grep -rn 'tmpdir' backend/src. The underlying hardening was still applied rather than argued away — the write uses flag:'wx' (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, does not follow a symlink) and 12 random bytes — which did NOT clear the alert, confirming the rule keys on something other than the exclusive-create gap.

Same false claim. The flagged write is the CACHE write, whose path is join(config.dataDir, 'pdf-cache') via routes/compliance.ts:54 — the configured data dir, not a shared temp dir. This file does use os.tmpdir() at line 94, but through mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'weaver-pdf-')), which is the CORRECT secure pattern (0700, kernel-generated random suffix) and is not the flagged line. Hardened anyway with flag:'wx' and 12 random bytes.
